root_idea.summary: A semantic orientation of spreading apart, separation, and loosening.
root_idea.development: The root develops from loosening wool or other compact material until it is spread out, and extends to ruffled feathers and animals dispersing to graze at night.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A distinct Quran-attested Form I verb, normalized from the inflected Quran form to its perfect-tense citation form.
A distinct Quran-attested passive participle, normalized from the inflected Quran form to its citation form.

senses.definition: Of flock animals: to disperse and pasture by night without a shepherd.
senses.usage_conditions: A nocturnal grazing and dispersal construction; the Quranic occurrence describes the people's sheep, which had wandered into cultivated growth.

senses.definition: Of wool or similar fibrous material: loosened and fluffed so that its fibers are spread apart.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic simile, wool is described in this loosened, separated, and expanded state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate, pluck apart, or loosen a compact thing so that it becomes spread, sparse, or dispersed; also, intransitively, to become so loosened and spread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of cotton, wool, and other material separated with the fingers; the intransitive use describes the resulting state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ruffle or spread the feathers around the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a cock or houbara when preparing to fight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become separated, loosened, spread, sparse, or dispersed, especially of cotton, wool, or similar material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive, quasi-passive counterpart to the transitive loosening expressed by نَفَشَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To let sheep, goats, or camels pasture by night without a shepherd, or to neglect them so that they disperse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction involving the release or neglect of grazing animals at night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bristle up the hair, or to ruffle or shake the feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of animals such as cats, hyenas, cocks, or birds, especially in fear, threat, or agitation.
A nominal use independent of the verbal action of loosening or spreading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A show of action where there is no actual action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative interpretation occurring in the cited proverb contrasting substance with appearance.
An alternative interpretation of the cited proverb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundance of speech, talk, or pretensions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage, including the sense of extravagant claims or verbal display.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proud or boastful person, especially one who praises himself for qualities he lacks or claims to have done what he has not done.
A large variety of citron or lemon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun for the specified fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal that pastures by night without a shepherd, especially a camel or sheep or goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle is also used in feminine and plural forms for such animals; the term distinguishes nocturnal unattended grazing from more general wandering.
Applied to a person characterized by untidy, bristling hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swollen or humid, and loose, flaccid, or soft within.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to anything having this swollen and internally soft or loose condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a nose: short in its soft front part and spreading over the face; of the nostrils, wide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical description of a broad, spreading nose or wide nostrils.

cautions: The Quranic Form I occurrence is the feminine singular perfect نَفَشَتْ, represented under the normalized citation form نَفَشَ.
The Quranic passive participle occurs in an inflected form, مَنْفُوشِ, represented under the citation form مَنْفُوشٌ.
The several interpretations of نَفَشٌ in the cited proverb are context-bound and should not be conflated with the ordinary noun wool.
